bugs.title: Checkout is returned to anyone who has its token
bugs.description: resolve_checkout looks a checkout up by token and returns it with no check of who is asking. The schema resolver drops info, so the requester is not even available. A token seen in a link, log or screenshot gives full read access to another customer's cart, address and email.
mechanism_anchors: no comparison of checkout.user with the requester
info is not passed to the resolver
a token is a bearer credential once it leaks
anonymous checkouts must stay readable by token
bugs.fix: Pass info to the resolver; return the checkout only if it is anonymous, owned by the requester, or the requester has the manage-checkouts permission (upstream PR #5268).

grader_instructions: Task-only example built from a real upstream bug. The multiple-choice parts are graded exactly; no judge is needed.
Upstream: issue saleor/saleor#5245, fixed by PR #5268.
Unrelated latent bug in the excerpt: CheckoutQueries.resolve_checkouts calls resolve_checkouts() without returning it. Not part of this task; do not penalize a note about it.

distractors.where.a: the argument type is fine; a UUID4 cannot be enumerated
distractors.where.d: resolve_checkout_lines is protected by permission_required in the schema
distractors.why.a: UUID4 values are random, not sequential
distractors.why.d: nothing in this code reuses tokens
distractors.fix.a: customers and anonymous shoppers could no longer read their own checkout; the storefront would break
distractors.fix.b: anonymous checkouts (user is None) and staff or apps would lose access
distractors.fix.c: longer tokens do not help once a token leaks; the missing ownership check remains
